name: Rhythms of grace
description: Seven days on simple habits that keep you close to God: Scripture, prayer, rest, worship, generosity and community.

days.title: Rooted like a tree
days.note: A picture of a life planted by water.
days.devotional:
The person who delights in God's word is like a tree by a stream, steady and fruitful in season.

Habits are how roots grow deep: small, daily, quiet.
days.prayer: Lord, plant me deep in Your word, so I grow steady and fruitful.
questions: What helps you delight in God's word?
When in your day could Scripture fit?

days.title: A quiet place
days.note: After a busy night, Jesus rises early to pray.
days.devotional:
Even Jesus, with crowds waiting, made space to be alone with the Father.

Prayer often needs a set time and place before it becomes natural.
days.prayer: Father, help me make a quiet place for You each day.
questions: Where could your quiet place be?
What usually crowds out prayer for you?

days.title: Rest
days.devotional:
The day of rest exists for people's good, Jesus says: a gift, not a burden.

Rest is an act of trust that the world keeps turning without our effort.
days.prayer: Lord, teach me to rest, and to trust You with what I leave undone.
questions: When did you last truly rest?
What would a weekly rhythm of rest look like for you?

days.title: Worship together
days.note: A call to keep meeting together.
days.devotional:
The writer urges believers not to give up meeting together, but to encourage one another.

Faith grows best with others beside us.
days.prayer: God, thank You for Your people. Help me show up and encourage someone.
questions: Whom could you encourage this week?

days.title: Fasting and the heart
days.note: Jesus speaks about giving, praying and fasting in secret.
days.devotional:
Jesus cares about why we do spiritual things. Done for God alone, even small acts are seen and rewarded by the Father.

Habits are about a heart turned towards God, not a performance.
days.prayer: Father, purify my motives. Let my habits be for You alone.
questions: Which habit do you do mostly for others' eyes?
What could you do in secret for God?

days.title: The fruit of the Spirit
days.note: Paul describes the character the Spirit grows.
days.devotional:
Love, joy, peace, patience and the rest of the Spirit's fruit grow as we walk with Him.

Habits make room; the Spirit makes the fruit.
days.prayer: Holy Spirit, grow Your fruit in me, especially where I'm weakest.
questions: Which fruit do you most want to grow?
What habit could make room for it?

days.title: Keep going
days.note: Paul encourages people not to grow tired of doing good.
days.devotional:
A harvest comes in its season to those who keep sowing. Spiritual habits are long obedience, not quick results.

If you missed days this week, just begin again.
days.prayer: Lord, help me keep going, and give me grace when I stumble.
questions: Which habit from this week will you keep?
What will help you begin again when you miss a day?
